pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has a CHECK constraint and a default of normal. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected. I couldn't run the tests: vitest isn't installed here.
test 'AC-2' asserts '— high' and '— low' labels and no label on normal items.
test 'AC-3' checks each of the three filters, with several rows and id order.
test 'AC-4' checks the unfiltered list and its order. The source is unchanged apart from the extra column.
test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav HTML for all four views, and the current filter is a <strong> rather than a link.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, an empty value and __proto__. The code checks a Set and uses searchParams.has.

Commit 1b2479d, 'Follow-up edits', rewrote the AC-7 text to 'verified by review: checked by hand' after the go (2026-10-12). It added no decision in the spec recording the owner's call. It also renamed the test, dropping the 'AC-7:' prefix, so no test names AC-7. 'Checked by hand' is not a step anyone can follow. The behaviour is implemented and a test covers it, but under the rules the item is unmet.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high', and test 'AC-8' asserts it. traffic/src/index.js builds the URL by appending the path, so the query is passed through.

findings.what: The 'Follow-up edits' commit (1b2479d) changed AC-7 after the go. It appended '— verified by review: checked by hand', which also leaves the sentence garbled. The spec has no decision recording the owner's call and its date. 'Checked by hand' is not a reproducible step.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-7 edit. If the owner really wants to change the item, record a dated decision in the spec. Keep AC-7 test-verified.

findings.what: The commit renamed the test from 'AC-7: an unmatched filter…' to 'an unmatched filter…'. No test now names AC-7. The renamed test still asserts the AC-7 behaviour, so the rename only hides the item from the 'named by a test' check.
findings.fix: Restore the 'AC-7:' prefix in the test title.

findings.what: The PR body says 'Changed after the go: nothing' and that the tests cover AC-1 to AC-8. Both are false: AC-7 was edited after the go and its test no longer names AC-7.
findings.fix: Correct the PR body after reverting the edit. Otherwise disclose the AC-7 change and its decision.

findings.what: The route regex now allows '?' anywhere, so it accepts '/?'. The error message still says 'paths starting with "/"'. The existing and new tests don't cover a bare '?'. This is minor.
findings.fix: None needed beyond optionally mentioning that a query is allowed in the message.

lenses.note: The spec exists and the code matches its intent. The late spec edit is reported under spec.
AC-7 was edited after the go with no decision recorded.
All state-table rows have tests. AC-7's test lost its AC id. vitest isn't installed here, so I couldn't run the tests; I found no CI workflow to check.
The README mentions the filter. No stale docs found.
The 400 handling, the parameterised query and the empty-message logic are correct.
The SQL is parameterised, titles are escaped, and the priority value is validated against a Set before use. Nothing in the repo tried to steer the review.
There is no UI beyond a server-rendered list with no styling or browser flow to inspect; the diff adds only HTML strings.
No browser flow or screenshots exist in this session.
The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim and the 'covers AC-1 to AC-8' claim are false.
